notes: LANDED 2026-09-02 (PB152). Action 1 is the consumer point 11.9.10.4 GR2/GR3/GR4 route to, and its ORDER against action 2 is structural: the fill is a BACKGROUND laid down first and then OVERWRITTEN by VALUE clauses, never a per-item substitute for a missing VALUE. pb152_options_initialize_background pins the ordering with an item that HAS a VALUE beside one that does not. No sequencing code was added - a field initializer is one expression, and only the expression's no-VALUE case changed - so the re-application sites (RecordStructEmitter's field initializers and __ResetStatics, the LOCAL-STORAGE per-activation re-seed, the OO instance cell) inherit it by construction. DETERMINATION recorded in CONFORMANCE.md and DATA_MODEL_DESIGN D23: 'the storage ... is set to the specified-fill-character' over a typed-native model means CHARACTER-FORMED storage takes the fill, while a NATIVE-NUMERIC carrier and an INDEX cell take their zero - licensed by 13.18.63.4 GR4 c), whose own sentence leaves a VALUE-less item 'undefined and set to a value that may or may not be allowed for that data item or index'. Class object/message-tag/pointer take NULL instead, because that same sentence states it as a positive requirement; USAGE BIT keeps its packed ceil(n/8) zero seed (D19) because its storage is packed bytes rather than character positions. EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED 2026-11-10: in force at 85 in part, for programs (functions and methods are not 1985 source units), §1985:X.2.4.2 GR1 'A program is in the initial state: (1) The first time the program is called in a run unit.'; this row's rule text is occasion 1 of §2023:14.6.2.3.2 while the notes above argue action 1 of its second list (the INITIALIZE fill, row GR-14.6.2.3.2-L2.1), the 2002 token rests on §2002:14.5.2.1.2.1 GR1, which prints the same sentence, and the 2014 token is forced by the validator and rests on no 2014 text read.
